1

Details

What changed since the 13 Oct version. The beam model was wrong: Lambda2D (lamda2DvsEn_EAR2.root) is the n_TOF resolution function, not a beam radius. The fit now uses the EAR2 beam from n_TOF's phase-4 FLUKA phase space through the EAR2 collimation (ear2_beam/, validated on the PPACMon beam-interception factors at 19.95 m to 1–2 %). The beam is about four times wider, so the "two readings" of the old version (and its ³He fractions) are void; the slides that depended on the old beam were removed. The data slides (track lines, pointing image, stability, late population, the A/C split) do not depend on the beam and are unchanged.

Fit: capsule_pose pose2 (A/C x crossings and x-vs-height shape), pose2z (D's z vs height), pose2d (A/C band-slope depth vs height, new 15 Oct). Report: <out>/capsule_pose_ear2/report.html.

The station, the capsule and the measured source, to scale

Hover the chambers, the capsule, the beam and the star. Dotted words and points everywhere carry tooltips.

geometry: run_config.json (survey), DetectorConstruction.cc polycones · beam: ear2_beam (EAR2 transport) × Phase-4 flux

2

Details

Frame. +y is the beam, vertical and up; +z points right (A), +x up (D) in this top-down view (COORDINATES.md). The origin is the surveyed station centre, which is also where the capsule is drawn (Geant4) and what the beam was aligned to. Each chamber's strip plane is 234.6 mm (A, C) or 234.1 mm (B, D) out and is shifted 15.5–17.3 mm sideways (the "pinwheel"), so no chamber is centred on the axis.

Capsule. The STEP polycones from MX17_Full_Geant: a 0.6 mm Al barrel (OD 21.2 mm) around 500 bar ³He, a 5.5 mm thick Al nose at the bottom (upstream), a 0.9 mm CFRP wrap. Beam neutrons that reach the ³He are absorbed within ~0.15 mm, so the gas is black: Al captures (the 7.7 MeV γ that make the tracks) happen where the beam first meets Al, before the gas.

Beam. The EAR2 beam at 19.5 m (n_TOF phase-4 phase space through the EAR2 collimation, ear2_beam/), late window, 1/v-weighted: 50 % inside r = 11.0 mm, 90 % inside 18 mm, 99 % inside 22 mm. (Until 14 Oct this slide drew Lambda2D, the resolution function, ~4× too narrow.)

The star is the measured source: x from chambers A and C, z from B and D, height from the y band crossing (scale-free; +y up).

Our old beam was the resolution function, ~4× too narrow

n_TOF's Lambda2D is λ (the moderation-length resolution), not a spot size; replaced on 14 Oct

A centred 20 mm bore now sees 46 % of the beam, not ~86 %.

The beam has a sharp edge at r ≈ 22 mm (the collimator image) and sits on the pipe axis to 1–2 mm.

Everything fitted on the old beam (the “two readings”) is void and has been refit.

ear2_beam/ (n_TOF phase-4 phase space, EAR2 collimation) · old: lamda2DvsEn_EAR2.root

3

Details

The histogram Lambda2D in MX17_Full_Geant/data/lamda2DvsEn_EAR2.root has its axis titled "lambda (cm)", is transport.cc's HIST_LAMBDA and sits beside its SAMMY resolution export: it is the distribution of the effective moderation length, used to build the time-of-flight resolution. The Geant4 gun and the first pose fit sampled it as a beam radius.

The real beam (ear2_beam/): n_TOF's phase-4 FLUKA phase space transported through the EAR2 collimation. Checked against the PPACMon beam-interception factors at 19.95 m to 1–2 %. At 19.5 m: r50 10.6 mm, r90 17.5 mm (late window, 1/v-weighted), sharp edge at ~22 mm. The thermal flux is the Phase-4 one (×1.19). Geant4 was rerun with this gun (condor 4454431/2, 19.5 and 19.95 m): ³He 0.448 per neutron (was ~0.95), Al 0.0028 (was 0.0045).

4

Details

Each line is one reconstructed track (gated, angle-calibrated, |tan| < 0.6, ≥ 20 ms), drawn from its chamber's strip plane through the axis plane z = 0 and a little beyond. Individual lines miss the source by ~25–40 mm: the γ converts or Compton-scatters in the capsule wall and air, and the electron scatters (Geant4: p·β·θ ≈ 0.4 MeV·rad). The ensemble still focuses, and the focus is the measurement.

Two estimators, same answer. The band crossing fits displacement-to-the-axis against position on the plane and takes the zero; it is scale-free (a wrong angle scale changes the slope, not the zero). The pointing excess (right) is the histogram of crossing points minus the same tracks with shuffled angles, which keeps the acceptance and destroys pointing; its peak survives background that ruins the band crossing before ~10 ms.

Chamber A's u axis points along +x and C's along −x, yet both find −10. A shift, a tan bias or a twist of one chamber would move the two images in opposite directions.

The pointing image is one compact spot left of the frame centre, at all times

chamber A, lines at the axis plane minus the shuffled-angle null, normalised per panel; white: the capsule as drawn

capsule_pose image.csv (A); +y = up

5

Details

Per window, a 2D histogram of where each line crosses the axis plane (x, height) minus the same with the x and y angles shuffled together among the tracks. The spot is elongated vertically because individual lines miss by ±25–40 mm in height (electron scattering, and the y angle scale is not calibrated); its centre is what the crossing estimators measure.

What is not there: a vertical ridge at the beam's x from captures along the beam line (¹⁴N(n,γ) in the air column gives 10.8 MeV γ at roughly the Al nose's rate per neutron), and a second spot near x = 0. Chamber C looks the same (image.csv).

It does not move: the same x from 2 to 75 ms, and in every run

left: pointing-excess peak per ToF bin (band crossing unusable < 10 ms) · right: per-run crossings

6

Details

Left. The excess peak is read with gain 1 on a point source (toy: −5 → −4.7, −10 → −9.7). Mixing the late data with a copy of itself moved +10 mm shifts it by 1.0 mm × fraction × 10, linearly (the grey lines). Diluting the late data with 1–2 ms tracks (mostly background) moves it by ≤ 2 mm. A beam centred on the frame with the capsule partly in it would put its own captures near x ≈ 0: at 2σ, at most 34 % (A) / 10 % (C) of the capsule tracks at 4–6 ms and 5 % at 6–12 ms come from there. A at 4–6 ms is the only bin that moves, and C in the same bin does not, so it is more likely background structure.

Right. The campaign-imaging crossings per run (production chain): post-access A -8.3 (s.d. 0.3), C -10.3 (0.5), D -3.5; pre-access A -9.5, C -10.3. The access did not move it. The production chain reads A ~2 mm closer to 0 than is2_v2; C agrees between chains.

7

Details

Frame (COORDINATES.md): +y is the beam, up; A at +z, C at −z, D at +x, B at −x. The tilt θ is from +y, toward the azimuth φ measured from +x toward +z, so φ = 135° puts the capsule top toward −x and +z: toward B and A. "Seen from C" looks along +z (x across); "seen from B" looks along +x (z across). Both side views and the top view share the scale in mm.

The pose shown is the minimum of χ²(A/C x crossings + A/C x-vs-height shape + D z-vs-height shape) over the grid: beam x ∈ {0, −5, −10}, capsule x −10…−20, θ 0–15°, φ in 45° steps; capsule z fixed at the B/D crossing (-3.8 mm); height not fitted but set by the y crossing (dy_c = -11.8 mm). The beam/capsule split sideways is degenerate (slide "sideways"): this picture is one member of that family.

The capture cloud is the toy: rays from the EAR2 beam walked through the posed STEP polycones, Al/CFRP capture ∝ 1/v with neutron scattering, the gas black. The measured source sits at the cloud's dense end on the nose, as it should: the pointing estimators measure where the Al captures are, not the capsule axis.

Higher up, the source sits further toward B: the top leans to −x

8

Details

Each point is the robust band crossing (where the tracks' lines cross the axis plane) of the tracks whose line reaches the axis plane at that height. A point source gives a flat curve; Geant4's untilted capsule is flat within ±1 mm. The toy curves are moved onto the data's overall crossing (x and y), so only the shape is compared: χ²_shape over the populated bins (−60…+20), with the Geant4-library bootstrap spread added to the data error.

The data's x moves ~4 mm toward −x from the bottom of the nose to above it, the same in A and C. A and C's u axes point opposite ways in global x, so a chamber-local error (strip map, tan bias) would split them, not move them together. What it cannot exclude by itself is a common in-plane rotation of the A–C pair; the z slides test the tilt with chambers that do not share that.

9

Details

D (the 14 Oct measurement): D's x view measures global z. Its band crossing per height bin, wall-coincident tracks only, ≥ 25 ms (below that D is junk). D's systematic: an in-plane rotation of D itself would tilt its curve; a ±3° rotation in the fit does not reorder the azimuths, but it is the one chamber.

A/C band-slope depth (new, 15 Oct; capsule_pose data_depth): A and C look along z, so they cannot see the source's z as a position, but they see it as a distance. A line from a source at depth w reaches a chamber at distance D_plane with displacement disp = −(pos − x_s)·D_plane/(D_plane − w): the band of (pos, disp) is steeper the closer the source is to the chamber. A source moving toward +z steepens A's band and flattens C's. So ln|slope_A| − ln|slope_C| per height bin is the source's z per height bin, up to a constant. A tan scale k common to all heights cancels (it only sets the constant), as does any height dependence that A and C share. The response, d(ln|a_A| − ln|a_C|)/dz = 0.0074 per mm (88 % of the ideal 2/234.6; the background dilutes it), is calibrated in each bin by moving every line of the sample by a known ±5 mm in z.

The two have different systematics. D's is a rotation of D; the A/C one's is a tan scale that depends on height differently in A and C (e.g. through tan y). They share no chamber, no estimator and no chain.

Caveat: the z and x shapes do not match one rigid tilt. The z rise happens below the source height (bins −80…−20; flat above), while the x drift toward B happens above it (−40…+20; flat or reversed below). A rigid tilt moves both along the whole capsule. So the lean's direction (its sign in x and in z) is well supported, by three measurements on two chamber pairs, but its size and shape are not: the toy matches the sign of D's rise, not its shape below the nose. A bent holder, a second source, or a height-dependent estimator bias are not excluded.

10

Details

For each measurement and each φ, the minimum χ² over the tilt θ (2–15°) and the beam/capsule positions in the grid. The x measurement (A/C crossings and x-vs-height shape) only knows the x component of the lean: it wants the top toward −x (φ 135–225) and cannot tell +z from −z. D's z vs height only knows the z component: it wants +z (φ 45–135) and cannot tell +x from −x. Only φ ≈ 135° satisfies both, which is what the combined curve shows.

The A/C band-slope depth is not in this χ²: its toy prediction (capsule_pose pose2d) is limited by the Geant4 library (≈10 k tracks per arm) to 2–3 mm per height bin, and its best χ² over φ varies by only 4.2. Its direct reading of the data (the previous slide) is what it contributes: the same +z half as D, from different chambers. Both z measurements will tighten with the EAR2-gun Geant4 library.

Sideways it is degenerate: ³He sees 20–53 % of the beam

best tilted pose for each beam position, from above, to scale; every one puts the captures on the measured source

11

Details

The x crossing measures where the Al captures are, which is where the beam meets the capsule: a beam on the frame with the capsule 16–20 mm off, and a beam 10 mm off with the capsule on it, put the captures at the same spot. The x-vs-height shape mildly prefers the beam off the frame (Δχ² ≈ 10–15), but that shape error is toy-library-limited, and n_TOF puts the beam on the pipe axis to 1–2 mm. If the frame is centred on the pipe, the first panel is the right one and the ³He sees ~0.2 of the beam at 19.5 m.

What would decide it: how the beam centring was done and against what; a photo or survey of the capsule against the beam axis; the beam spot at the station. The 19.95 m beam gives the same picture (beam-centred family χ² 35, ³He 0.23; beam −5/−10: 29, 0.34–0.41).

Most capsule tracks come after the beam, yet they image the same nose spot

left: arrival time of capsule-pointing tracks vs expected beam captures · right: source height vs ToF

capsule_tof tof.csv / beam_capture.csv · capsule_pose tof.csv

12

Details

Left. 87 % of the beam's own captures (EAR2 flux × 1/v) fall before 12 ms, peaking at 5–6 ms; 92 % of the tracks that point at the capsule are after 12 ms and half after 30 ms (recorded rates, DAQ-limited, so only the shape means anything). The ≥ 30 ms trigger rate falls with T½ ≈ 24 ms, read in the tracking handoff (§10f) as the die-away of thermalised neutrons in the EAR2 hall.

Right. Those late tracks image the nose (−31 / −35) and the same x. An isotropic hall flux would light the whole capsule body and put the source at y ≈ +5 to +8. So whatever illuminates the capsule late is narrow and on the nose, like a beam, which is not understood; it is also why the direct-beam test cannot isolate the beam: the 4–12 ms capsule tracks are a mixture whose beam share is unknown.

Before 12 ms the height drops; that follows the purity drop and no pose moves the beam window down, so it is read as an unsubtracted beam-line source below the capsule.

A misplaced chamber cannot fake this: it would split A and C

the A and C x views point opposite ways in global x

A and C agree (-10.1 / -10.7 mm), so the offset is not a strip-map, angle or alignment error of one chamber. The same holds for B and D in z (−4.1 / −3.5).

What survives is a shift of the whole A–C pair (and B–D pair) against the beam. That is exactly the beam-vs-frame question.

The scintillators cannot test it: the SiPM wall sits within 1–6 mm of the survey, but wall and chambers share one structure.

The x sign was fixed by this same split (2026-08-20): a wrong sign splits A and C by twice the ~16 mm pinwheel.

13

Details

U_HAT is +x for A and −x for C (ntof_tracking/reco/geometry.py). Any error that lives in a chamber's own coordinates — the strip-map centre (STRIP_MAP_HALF), a constant tan offset, a yaw about y, or a sign — therefore moves the two images in opposite global directions. Their agreement to 0.5 mm (is2_v2) bounds those to well below the 10 mm offset. The production chain reads A ~2 mm closer to 0 than is2_v2; that is the chain systematic.

The chamber centres in run_config.json are the survey's (pinwheel shifts 15.5 / 15.75 / 16.35 / 17.3 mm; MX17_Full_Geant docs/HANDOFF_ARM_GEOMETRY.md). A common shift of both A and C (A's pinwheel 10 mm smaller, C's 10 mm larger) is invisible to every internal check.

What this does not rule out, and what would settle it

not ruled out

  • Where the beam is relative to the frame: the sideways split is degenerate, and it sets the ³He yield ×3.
  • Faking the lean needs a common rotation of the A–C pair (x) and, for z, both a twist of D and an A/C tan-scale asymmetry with height, of the right sizes.
  • The tilt's size and shape: z moves below the source height, x above it; one rigid tilt fits neither shape well (a bent holder or a second source would).
  • The toy's shapes are Geant4-library-limited (≈10 k tracks per arm, July Lambda2D gun).
  • Why the after-the-flux (20–75 ms) population images the nose like the beam does.
